A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SVG work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original image reconstruction and generation experiments, encoder ablations, downstream classification, segmentation and depth results, and editing and interpolation demonstrations.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds encoder-layer experiments, tokenizer efficiency measurements, guidance analyses, and higher-resolution generation demonstrations.

M1.justification: The frozen DINOv3 encoder, residual encoder, distribution alignment, decoder, and flow-matching pipeline are retained. Equation (6) specifies the existing alignment component rather than establishing a changed algorithm. Appendix H explicitly reports higher-resolution adaptation without architectural modifications.

E1.justification: Appendix H extends demonstrated generation coverage from 256×256 to 512×512 and 1024×1024, supported by Figures 15–18; v1 left higher-resolution generation to future work. The datasets, semantic domains, and downstream tasks otherwise remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The main generation comparator roster is unchanged, including the already-present REPA-XL row. Comparator participation expands in diagnostic evaluations: Figure 4 supplies VA-VAE, SD-VAE and MAR-VAE linear-probe comparisons, while Table 7 directly compares SVG tokenizer modules with SD-VAE, VA-VAE and DINOv3.

E3.justification: Substantial additional protocols accompany the new analyses: intermediate-layer evaluation using SVG-B at 200K steps with 5/20-epoch autoencoders; tokenizer latency at batch size 1 and throughput at 64; guidance sweeps comparing constant CFG and zero initialization; and staged fine-tuning at 512×512 and 1024×1024. These supplement the retained experimental settings rather than establish reruns of existing results.

E4.justification: v4 adds intermediate-layer reconstruction/generation experiments and alignment-related latent visualizations (Appendix E), tokenizer cost analysis (Appendix F), guidance sensitivity comparisons (Figure 13), and convergence curves across model sizes (Figure 14). These investigate feature semantics, efficiency, sampling sensitivity and training stability beyond v1's retained component ablations, interpolation tests and PCA visualizations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates. The added curves and tables do not introduce such reporting; references to random image or noise sampling are not repeated-run statistics.

E6.justification: The headline SVG scores remain unchanged. Table 1 fills the 80-epoch REPA-XL row with unguided IS 118.6, guided gFID 2.65 and guided IS 268.62. v4 also adds VAE linear-probe accuracies, layer-specific gFIDs of 73.45, 36.63 and 27.00 in Table 6, tokenizer measurements, guidance/convergence curves and higher-resolution samples. These are additional results, not matched-setting improvements over v1's SVG scores.

T1.justification: Equation (6) newly gives an explicit mathematical definition of residual-feature alignment through DINO mean and standard-deviation matching, previously described verbally. The diffusion, flow-matching and interpolation mathematics otherwise remain substantively unchanged, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same principal claims: a VAE-free SVG representation supports efficient diffusion training, few-step generation and preserved downstream capabilities. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly explains the layer experiment through shallow texture features versus deeper semantic abstraction. Appendix F interprets tokenizer costs as supporting batch scalability despite latency differences, and Appendix H extends the stated applicability to higher resolutions without architectural changes. The original limitations paragraph remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 specifies the alignment normalization, adds project-page and code-repository links, and documents checkpoints and fine-tuning schedules for the higher-resolution experiments. The existing hyperparameter table, training hardware and downstream implementation details are retained. The PDFs establish the added access information, but not the external resources' contents or availability.

R1.justification: The visual-generation related-work passage expands to latent-space regularization, diffusion autoencoders and joint image-feature generation, adding works including EQ-VAE, Preechakul et al., Pandey et al. and Wu et al. The introduction also replaces its criticism about unchanged VAE training objectives with a narrower semantic-discriminability criticism. The overall novelty positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Editing is localized: abstract and introduction wording is refined, related work is expanded, Section 3.3 is renamed, and acknowledgments and additional appendix sections appear. Publication and corresponding-author information are updated. Most existing method, experimental and conclusion prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned with a representation legend, expanded caption and corrected training/inference panel descriptions. Figure 4 gains accuracy annotations. Two new tables and new latent-space, guidance, convergence and higher-resolution figures substantially expand the visual evidence. Existing main-text displays are redistributed; the retained interpolation, PCA and sample-gallery figures are matched across renumbering.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens evidence for the central semantic-structure and efficiency arguments. Quantitative linear probes and the controlled encoder-layer study supplement v1's qualitative embeddings and toy example, while Table 7 makes tokenizer costs assessable and exposes the throughput versus single-image latency tradeoff. The alignment formula improves methodological clarity, and guidance analyses test an acknowledged weakness. These gains improve the support and assessability of the paper despite unchanged headline SVG scores. Higher-resolution evidence remains qualitative, and statistical uncertainty is still unreported.
